questions.q: How does Claude Desktop know which MCP servers to launch and connect to?
options: It automatically connects to every MCP server on the internet
It cannot connect to any servers without a paid plan
By scanning the local network for open ports
Through a JSON configuration file (claude_desktop_config.json) listing each server and how to launch it
questions.explain: Claude Desktop reads a config file at a known location declaring which servers to start automatically and how to launch each one.

questions.q: Once a client connects to a server, how does it learn what tools that server offers?
options: Through the discovery step: calling tools/list (and resources/list, if relevant) to get back the server's tool definitions
It doesn't — the host developer must hardcode the list in advance
By guessing based on the server's name
The server emails a PDF list of its tools
questions.explain: Discovery happens automatically right after connection — the client asks the server what it offers via protocol operations like tools/list, rather than anything being hardcoded ahead of time.

questions.q: In the Plan, Act, Observe agent loop from earlier in this course, what does connecting to an MCP server actually change?
options: It replaces the entire loop with a new MCP-specific loop
It removes the Observe step entirely
It changes where the tools available at the Act step can come from — discovered from a server, not only hardcoded in your own code — without changing the loop itself
It eliminates the need for a Plan step
questions.explain: MCP doesn't introduce a new loop; it changes the source of the tools available during Act, which can now include tools discovered from a connected server.

questions.q: If a host connects to two different MCP servers at once, what does the model see when deciding which tool to call?
options: Two completely separate conversations, one per server
One combined set of available tools to choose from, even though they came from two separate client connections behind the scenes
Only the tools from whichever server connected first
The model cannot use tools from more than one server at a time
questions.explain: The protocol keeps each client-server connection and its discovered tools straight internally, but from the model's point of view at the Act step, it's one pooled set of tools to select from — the same selection problem covered in the tool-routing lesson.

questions.q: What real example server does this lesson use to illustrate a local MCP connection, and what capability does it add to Claude Desktop?
options: A weather server that adds stock market data
A server that removes the need for human approval entirely
The Filesystem Server, which adds tools for reading, creating, and searching local files — each action requiring explicit approval
A server that only works on Linux
questions.explain: The official Filesystem Server is a real, documented example: once configured, it gives Claude Desktop tools for file access, with every action still requiring the user's explicit approval.
